Confirmed — that's not you missing a mechanic, it's baked into freighter bases: you can't place generators, batteries, or power sources like you can on a planetary base. Power on a freighter comes automatically from the freighter itself and radiates out room-by-room (each room/corridor has its own connection bubble, roughly ~4 units), rather than something you generate and route with wires. So there's no build option that's actually missing — freighters just don't do custom power generation at all, only distribution.

The dead-zone frustration you're hitting is a known layout quirk: stairs and disconnected sections don't reliably pass power along even when everything looks physically connected, while stacked corridors or ladders usually do. So the lights failing isn't (always) about total power draw — it's often about a room being just outside its neighbor's power bubble, especially anything built up or across levels rather than radiating straight out from the bridge.

Given how much you've built already, if you've got dead zones you actually want lit, running a ladder connection (even just a decorative stub) between the powered and unpowered sections is the most reported fix, more reliable than stairs.

Confirmed — that's not you missing a mechanic, it's baked into freighter bases: you can't place generators, batteries, or power sources like you can on a planetary base. Power on a freighter comes automatically from the freighter itself and radiates out room-by-room (each room/corridor has its own connection bubble, roughly ~4 units), rather than something you generate and route with wires. So there's no build option that's actually missing — freighters just don't do custom power generation at all, only distribution.

The dead-zone frustration you're hitting is a known layout quirk: stairs and disconnected sections don't reliably pass power along even when everything looks physically connected, while stacked corridors or ladders usually do. So the lights failing isn't (always) about total power draw — it's often about a room being just outside its neighbor's power bubble, especially anything built up or across levels rather than radiating straight out from the bridge.

Given how much you've built already, if you've got dead zones you actually want lit, running a ladder connection (even just a decorative stub) between the powered and unpowered sections is the most reported fix, more reliable than stairs.

The Dreadnought is the most visually complex freighter in the game, with it being the latest model since the Sentinel and Capital ships. The textures are the same used on the newest space stations from the Orbital update. It has multiple glowing fins at the bottom, resembling the oars of a classic Viking longship. The Dreadnought Warp Drive consists of 4 engines that can be destroyed. When the hull is under 30% and/or all anti-freighter cannons have been destroyed, the Dreadnought will attempt to charge its warp drive (which takes about 33 seconds) and warp to another star system; if all four of the engines have been destroyed then the Dreadnought will immediately surrender instead. The Dreadnought is equipped with 10 shield generators to protect itself from attacks, hidden in a pair of trenches on either side of the ship's central axis. Each shield generator generates 10% shield power.

There are a total of 6 large anti-freighter laser turrets, 1 in the front of the ship and 5 near the rear, and many small heat cannons scattered around the hull. During the pirate battle, the anti-freighter lasers will do about 1% damage to the civilian fleet per shot. On lower difficulties, the heat cannons can be ignored as they will not need to be destroyed - unless the player is sick of getting shot at. On higher difficulties, however, the player may need to destroy these in order to sufficiently damage the freighter for its surrender or destruction. When owned by a player, the freighter will use its weapons in combat against the player's enemies, including firing the anti-freighter lasers at hostile capital ships. The lasers won't deal any damage while shields are up, but once that is dealt with, they can one-shot the exposed hull of even a Sentinel Capital Ship.

(Note that the Carrier AI Fragment item will not drop if the Dreadnought is the one that destroys the capital ship.) ... Pirate Frigates are a type of frigate in No Man's Sky that can be obtained after defeating the Pirate Dreadnought they accompany. They become available for purchase whether the player destroys the Dreadnought or forces its surrender, but if the player decides to seize the freighter after its surrender then they will disappear. Pirate Frigates are labeled as "raiding specialists", being armed to the teeth and perfect for dangerous missions that other frigates might not survive, but otherwise behave like regular combat frigates. They can be sent on expeditions like all frigates, and you can buy, repair, fuel, level up, and use them. They can also be damaged during high-difficulty expeditions like all frigates, so sending them together with other frigates is still the best way to go.

The Dreadnought flees the battle. If the player has destroyed all 6 of the anti-freighter lasers or has dealt at least 70% damage to the ship's hull, and if at least one of the ship's 4 engines are still intact, then the freighter will begin to charge its warp engines. Charging takes around 33 seconds, at which point the freighter will warp out of the system. ... The Dreadnought surrenders. This will happen if the freighter wishes to flee the battle (because its lasers were destroyed and/or it received 70% hull damage) but is unable to (because its 4 engines have been destroyed). The battle ends the moment it surrenders: in-flight torpedoes will disappear. The pirate frigates will warp away if the player seizes the Dreadnought, so they should be hired before landing if they need to be hired. ... Additionally, the player can seize the Dreadnought or extort Units from the captain, as well as hire away the Frigates ·

The 4 warp drive engines sit on the underside of the Dreadnought's rear section, below the main deck. You fly underneath the ship toward the back, get under its shield coverage, and shoot the engines out from that angle — no need to punch through the shield dome from the top for this part.

Priority order given you'll have your own freighter helping:

1. **First, thin out the escort** — let your freighter and any wingmen handle frigates/torpedoes while you focus the Dreadnought itself, since a stray torpedo can one-shot the civilian freighter you need alive.
2. **Destroy the 4 warp engines** (underside rear) early — this is what locks it in place so it can't flee once it takes enough damage.
3. **Then hit the shield generators** — they're in two trenches running down either side on top of the main deck, so you fly into the trench to expose them.
4. **Once shields are down, exposed fuel rods pop up in the same trench locations** — destroy those for real hull damage.
5. Once its engines are gone and either hull is at 70%+ or all 6 anti-freighter lasers are destroyed, it surrenders instead of trying to flee — that's your cue to fly in, dock, and find the captain on the bridge to seize it.

One important sequencing note worth flagging: don't disable the warp drives *before* softening the shields/lasers if you're gunning for the full reward path — some reports say attacking the engines too early with the ship still at high hull can mess with the surrender trigger versus fleeing behavior. Safest order is escort clear → shields/lasers down → engines last, so it can't run right when it's about to break.
